content:
alex: 🚨 FYI customer CUST-482 (Prod Dedicated) reporting bursts of 429s + elevated latency since ~03:00 UTC. Ticket #8764. They say traffic volume hasn't changed on their side.

mira: Which pool/tenant? Any recent config changes? logs or example headers would help.

alex: Tenant t-482 on dedicated-pool-12. Here's one error header from the tenant proxy: `x-rate-limit-reason: tenant_quota_exceeded`, `x-tenant-usage: 78/80` — but their observed QPS suggests we should be under cap. Attaching small repro curl they sent: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","input":"hello"}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

sam: ops-bot shows a config change at 02:58 UTC affecting quota mappings for tenants. Automation PR 2117 applied a unit-normalization change. I'm seeing the mapping convert `per_minute` -> `per_minute` but the limiter reads `per_second`. If that's true, effective limit = intended_limit / 60.

ops-bot: [config-change] PR 2117 merged by automation-bot at 2026-03-16T02:58:12Z. Changed tenant quota normalization: `units: minute` -> `units: minute` (normalized).

mira: That would explain it. Customer thought they had 300 QPS; if config interpreted as per_minute it's now 5 QPS.

eli: I put a temporary tenant override: t-482 -> quota 18000/sec (bypass) at 03:10 UTC so customer is unblocked. Notified on ticket. We need a config rollback or hotfix.

mike: Autoscaler note: even before override, dedicated-pool-12 had spare GPUs but autoscaler didn't spin new nodes because we short-circuit scaling when per-tenant throttles return 429s — autoscaler thinks it's not capacity-constrained. That's an orthogonal bug: throttle should not suppress scale triggers.

jessica: Cross-team plan: 1) revert normalization in PR 2117 (infra) 2) patch rate-limiter to treat unit mapping explicitly and validate 3) fix autoscaler detection so 429s from quota don't block node scaling when request backlog increases. Who owns each?

sam: I can revert PR 2117 now and push a fix in the morning to normalize mapping to `per_second` canonical form. Planning rollback at 03:40 UTC.

mira: Eng-runtime for change to throttle->scale signal: @mike can you open a P1 for that? Include replay steps and logs.

mike: Opening ENG-RUNTIME-462: include heap of request traces and counterexamples. Will prioritize after rollback.

eli: Noted, customer updated and historically they hit a spike from a cron job at 02:55 UTC which coincided with PR deploy. We have overlap of noisy-neighbor + misconfigured quota units.

alex: Customer still seeing single-digit errors after override but overall service is functional. They asked for postmortem and ETA for permanent fix.

jessica: Assigning owners: infra (sam) for immediate revert + unit test, runtime (mike) for autoscaler signal, support (eli/alex) for customer comms and Jira for postmortem. I'll add a follow-up in #postmortems.

mira: For the postmortem please include: repro steps, diff of PR 2117, unit test gap, and rollout gating for future quota changes.

sam: Revert rolled at 03:42 UTC, PR 2130. I also added a validation check to reject unit values except `per_second`/`per_minute` with explicit mapping and a warning. That should land in canary in 10m.

ops-bot: [deploy] PR 2130 deployed to canary at 03:52 UTC.

mike: ENG-RUNTIME-462 created and assigned to runtime oncall, description includes backlog traces and a small reproducer.

eli: Closing the customer ticket as mitigated, will keep them posted on permanent fixes.

alex: Thanks all. We'll follow up with a short blameless postmortem and add a runbook item for quota-unit deploys. :thumbsup:
